data.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 28 at 5:39AM EDT until October 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 PM this evening to 8 PM
EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
data.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

FXUS62 KMFL 281059
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
659 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 657 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

 - Major coastal flooding is expected during high tide today, with
   moderate flooding into the end of this week. Inundated roadways
   are expected for coastal areas.

 - Marine and beach conditions will remain hazardous today, but
   improving conditions are expected for the end of this week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Thursday)
Issued at 222 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

South Florida will remain on the periphery of a mid-level low 
centered near the Bahamas that will begin to weaken and advect 
northeastwards away from the area for the end of this week. A nearby 
surface low is also analyzed early this morning that can provide 
some extra forcing for ascent in the low-levels, but any convection 
today will be capped as lapse rates are weak and mid-level temps are 
several degrees above normal (500mb temps at -3 to -4 deg C). In 
addition, an abundance of dry air is present on the latest ACARS 
soundings and model soundings, which combined with a rebuilding 
ridge heading into Thursday will further cap convective and 
lightning potential. With the ridge amplifying and the low offshore 
beginning to advect northeastward, the channel of strongest winds 
will shift north of the South Florida forecast area and thus much 
less windy conditions are expected through the period, but they are 
likely to still be on the breezier side for today.

Overall, while some shallow isolated to scattered shower activity 
along with very low-end chances for a thunderstorm or two. 
Thunderstorms are unlikely with this atmospheric profile, but can 
never rule out a single more robust updraft occurring that allows 
for deep enough convection to spark a pulse storm. Regardless, from 
a general weather perspective both today and tomorrow, concerns are 
limited with no major hazards expected. High temperatures will rise 
a few degrees as high pressure builds and more sunshine is possible, 
so temperatures will reach the mid to upper 80s. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Thursday night through Tuesday)
Issued at 222 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

This forecast features no tricks, but honestly, not too much in the 
form of treats either as Halloween in South Florida is forecast to 
be close to normal for this time of year. Warm daytime temperatures 
will drop into the upper 70s to low 80s during the evening hours, 
with a 30-50% chance of coastal showers along the east coast of 
South Florida and a light but not spooky easterly breeze. But before 
I haunt you any further with my forecast, let's rewind back to the 
beginning of the extended period. 

The atmospheric reign of the cut-off low that has resided to our 
east over the northwestern Bahamas and western Atlantic waters over 
the last several days will finally conclude. While zonal mid-level 
flow will prevail across much of the southeastern United States, a 
developing mid-level ridge across the southern Gulf will slide 
eastward during the second half of the week, resulting in increasing 
geopotential heights, 500mb temperatures above the 90-95th 
percentile, and a reduction in 500mb wind speeds out of the 
northwest. At the surface, the weak area of surface low vorticity is 
forecast continue to meander westward across the region, 
increasingly decoupled from the departing cut-off low. An associated 
frontal boundary, increasingly diffuse and meager in nature, will 
also retrograde across the region during the second half of the 
week. While this boundary will gradually degrade, the envelope of 
deeper atmospheric moisture will remain across the region with 
precipitable water values in the 80th-90th percentile forecast to 
remain draped across the region. The pressure gradient that has kept 
a persistent breeze across the region will finally abate with high 
temperatures in the mid to upper 80s across most of South Florida, 
with even some low 90s possible across inland southwestern Florida 
through the upcoming weekend. While winds will continue to lessen 
across the region, there will be enough of an easterly wind 
component to create a minor temperature gradient across the region 
with the warmest overnight temperatures forecast along the east 
coast and warmest daytime temperatures across inland southwestern 
Florida as oceanic influences keep temperatures warmer overnight but 
cooler during the day. Warm 500mb temperatures and ridging aloft 
will keep convection fairly benign in nature through the first half 
of the weekend with convection mainly focusing across inland 
southwestern Florida on the confluence of a stronger Atlantic sea-
breeze and weaker Gulf breeze. 

Mid-level ridging across our region is forecast to erode during the 
second half of the weekend into early next week as a lobe of mid-
level vorticity slides eastward across the southeastern United 
States in tandem with a developing surface low and frontal boundary. 
Ample warm air and moisture advection is forecast to occur mainly to 
the north of our region during this time frame, with the best 
atmospheric dynamics and ascent over the northern half of the 
Florida Peninsula and remainder of the southeastern United States. 
That being said, a cooling of 500mb temperatures and a more 
southerly component to surface winds could focus a higher chance of 
convection across inland South Florida on Sunday as moisture lifts 
northwards in the expansive warm sector of the system to our north. 
Beyond early next week, ensemble and deterministic guidance have a 
great variety of potential forecast solutions as the southern stream 
remains active across the southern United States. In the near term 
however, it looks like South Florida will have to wait longer for 
the treat of a substantial cold front and pumpkin spice
conditions.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 657 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

SCT to BKN MVFR ceilings this morning. NE winds around 5 kts early
this morning increasing slightly to 10-15 kts late morning through
the afternoon. Light and variable winds overnight. Scattered
showers possible throughout the day.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 222 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Conditions begin to improve today, but lingering Small Craft 
Advisory conditions are expected into this evening and tonight 
before tapering off across the Gulf and Atlantic waters. Northeast 
winds at 20-25 kts in the Gulf and seas of 7-10 feet are expected in 
the Gulf and Atlantic respectively into tonight before falling off. 
Winds fall to moderate levels tomorrow while veering more easterly. 
Conditions for the end of the week will become more calm. Isolated 
to scattered shower activity remains likely as well at least for the 
next few days.

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 222 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

A high risk of rip currents will persist for all Atlantic beaches 
through today before tapering off for the Broward and Miami-Dade 
beaches this evening. However, a high risk for rip currents will 
continue through at least Thursday for the Palm Beaches. Surfing 
conditions will also be improving today for the Palm Beaches, but 
waves of 7-8 feet will still be possible through today which keeps 
the High Surf Advisory in effect until tonight. 

Furthermore, onshore wind flow and high seas combined with King 
Tides will result in another day of increased coastal flooding risk 
along the Atlantic coast. The tides could still reach major flood 
stage again today, but then are expected to fall for the end of the 
week. However, moderate flooding is still expected during periods of 
high tide through at least Thursday or Friday, so a Coastal Flood 
Advisory will take over for when the Warning expires.

&&
